mnemonic: 바람 = a gust of wind: something sudden knocks your plans over, and the damage is already done.
meaning: because of a sudden, unexpected event, with an unwanted result ("…, and so I ended up …")
nuance: The cause is a sudden or unforeseen event, and its (usually unwanted) result has already happened. The form is always -는, even for past events: 넘어지는 바람에, not *넘어진 바람에. The main clause is normally past tense and cannot be a command or suggestion (-(으)세요, -자, -(으)ㅂ시다). The tone is neutral: it reports what happened without blaming anyone or describing the atmosphere. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 126.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 points a finger: the cause is held responsible. -는 바람에 just reports a sudden cause.
-는 통에 blames a hectic, chaotic scene (noise, crowds, commotion); -는 바람에 is one sudden event.

examples.ko: 지하철이 중간에 멈추는 바람에 면접에 20분이나 늦었다.
examples.en: The subway stopped partway, so I ended up a full 20 minutes late for my interview.

examples.ko: 급하게 나오는 바람에 지갑을 집에 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: I left in such a rush that I forgot my wallet at home.

cloze.sentence: 버스에서 깜빡 {{}} 내릴 정류장을 지나쳐 버렸어요.
cloze.en: I nodded off on the bus and missed my stop.

nearMiss.hint: 졸다 drops its ㄹ before -는: 조는.
-는 바람에 stays -는 even for a past event: 조는 바람에.
-는 통에 needs a hectic, chaotic scene. Nodding off is one sudden slip, and the cue asks for -는 바람에.

nuance.situation: 밖에 비가 쏟아지기 시작했는데 친구가 막 나가려고 해요. 우산을 가져가라고 말하려면? (It has started pouring and your friend is about to head out. You tell them to take an umbrella.)

options.why: -는 바람에 reports a result that has already happened. It can't lead into a command.
-(으)니까 gives a reason and can be followed by a command or suggestion.
Same problem: -는 통에 explains something that already went wrong, so no command can follow it.

mnemonic: 탓 = fault, as in "네 탓이야!" The clause is the finger you point at the cause.
meaning: because of (a cause blamed for a bad outcome); "owing to", "thanks to" in the sarcastic sense
nuance: 탓 means fault or blame, so the clause names a cause held responsible for a negative outcome. Unlike -는 바람에, it takes past (-(으)ㄴ) and adjective forms, and the cause can be a lasting condition rather than a sudden event. It is never used for good outcomes; for those, use 덕분에. Common in both speech and news writing. 탓 also stands alone as a noun: 날씨 탓이다, 남 탓을 하다.

contrasts.note: -는 바람에 neutrally reports a sudden event and only takes -는; -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 assigns blame and also takes past and adjective forms.
-는 통에 is specifically about commotion; -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 can blame any cause, including a person or a steady condition.

examples.ko: 평소에 운동을 게을리한 탓에 계단 몇 층만 올라가도 숨이 찬다.
examples.en: Because I've neglected exercise, I get winded after just a few flights of stairs.

examples.ko: 일교차가 큰 탓에 감기 환자가 늘고 있다.
examples.en: Cold cases are rising because of the wide swings between daytime and nighttime temperatures.

nuance.situation: 친구가 추천해 준 식당이 정말 맛있었어요. 친구에게 고마운 마음을 전하려면? (The restaurant your friend recommended was great. You want to thank them.)

options.text: 네가 추천해 준 탓에 정말 잘 먹었어.
options.why: -(으)ㄴ 탓에 blames a cause for a bad result. Here it sounds sarcastic, as if the meal were a disaster.

options.text: 네가 추천해 준 덕분에 정말 잘 먹었어.
options.why: 덕분에 credits a cause for a good result.

options.text: 네가 추천해 주는 통에 정말 잘 먹었어.
options.why: -는 통에 needs a chaotic situation and an unwanted result.

register.source: 제가 확인을 제대로 안 한 탓에 일정이 늦어졌어요.
accepted: 제가 확인을 제대로 안 한 탓에 일정이 늦어졌습니다.
제가 확인을 제대로 하지 않은 탓에 일정이 늦어졌습니다.

mnemonic: Picture yourself stuck in the thick of a noisy crowd: with all that going on, you couldn't do what you meant to.
meaning: because of a hectic or chaotic situation (noise, crowds, commotion), with an unwanted result ("what with all the …")
nuance: 통 here is the thick of things: the cause is a busy, noisy, or confused situation, often an ongoing one, that got in the way. The result is unwanted and has already happened, so no command or suggestion can follow. It is more colloquial than -는 바람에 and -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 and often carries a note of irritation.

contrasts.note: Both take -는 and report an unwanted result. -는 바람에 is one sudden event (the bus stopped); -는 통에 is a whole messy scene (kids yelling, construction all day).
-(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 assigns blame to any cause; -는 통에 is specifically about commotion.

examples.ko: 윗집 아이들이 밤늦게까지 뛰어다니는 통에 한숨도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: What with the kids upstairs running around till late, I didn't sleep a wink.

examples.ko: 다들 한꺼번에 떠드는 통에 무슨 얘긴지 하나도 못 알아들었다.
examples.en: Everyone was talking at once, so I couldn't make out a thing.

cloze.sentence: 옆 사무실에서 하루 종일 {{}} 통화를 제대로 할 수가 없었어요.
cloze.en: With the office next door under construction all day, I couldn't hold a proper phone call.

nearMiss.hint: Grammatical, but the cue asks for -는 통에: an all-day racket is exactly the ongoing commotion -는 통에 describes.
